extracted.intended_audience: business journalists, editors, freelancers, and students preparing submissions for the SABEW Best in Business awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and category definitions for submitting work to the SABEW (Society for Advancing Business Editing and Writing) Best in Business contest, including eligibility, element limits, category definitions, and cover letter requirements for professional and student entrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of contest categories (2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are 29 contest categories in 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories are broken out by size divisions, determined by the news organization’s total, distinct editorial staff: Small: 50 or less editorial staff; Medium: 51-150 editorial staff; Large: 151+ editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations compete against other similarly sized organizations, regardless of format. Freelancers will be grouped based on the size of the outlet that published their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry publications handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry/Topic-specific publications will have an additional General Excellence category and otherwise compete against similarly sized news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry publications get an extra General Excellence category; otherwise they are grouped by the size divisions above.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Excellence — submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one entry per publication is allowed in this category. A cover letter of up to 400 words may be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should showcase the depth and breadth of quality in your publication. Entrants must demonstrate general excellence by submitting at least one element from four of the five specified areas of coverage and may submit up to five elements. Stories submitted for this award can also be submitted in a story type or story topic category.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Excellence — required coverage areas (scoop/breaking/explanatory/investigative/visual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must submit at least one element from four of five areas: Scoop; Breaking news; Explanatory/Feature; Investigative Project; Visual Storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may submit up to five elements total. For some element types (e.g., Breaking news, Investigative Project), entrants are encouraged to include explanatory material in the cover letter (e.g., full day’s coverage plan, overall package description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoop (as an element)
rubrics_metrics.description: A news story exclusive to your publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be submitted as one element to satisfy General Excellence requirements; may also be entered in relevant story type or story topic categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News (element / story type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage within the first 24 hours of a breaking story, demonstrating speed of delivering headlines, stories and analysis with relevant context and value-added information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants in this category can submit up to five stories, segments or short-form alerts (when submitted in the Breaking News story type). All items submitted must include timestamps and the entry should include a reference to the time the news originally became public. For General Excellence, entrants are encouraged to include in their cover letter a description of the full day’s coverage plan to give broader context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory (story type / element)
rubrics_metrics.description: In-depth reporting that presents, analyzes and simplifies a single important topic and/or news event in a way that allows audiences to understand it more clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be submitted as an element for General Excellence or as its own story type entry. Avoid conflating with Feature — explanatory emphasizes analysis and clarification of a single topic/event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature (story type / element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enterprise storytelling that may be presented as a trend story, a profile or a narrative, that draws on in-depth reporting to offer fresh discovery or insight in a memorable way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature emphasizes narrative, profiles or trend-driven enterprise reporting offering fresh insight; can be used as an element in General Excellence or entered as a story type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative Project (element / story type)
rubrics_metrics.description: In-depth reporting that: a) presents important and vital information largely unknown to the audience and unavailable from other sources before publication; and b) demonstrates an obvious need for change in law/policy/behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For General Excellence, entrants are encouraged to include in their cover letter a description of the overall package. Investigative entries should establish novelty of findings and show impact/need for change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual Storytelling (element)
rubrics_metrics.description: A stand-alone visual story — could be a video, a series of related photographs or an interactive data visualization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual story elements count toward General Excellence and may also be entered in the Video or Data categories as appropriate. Visuals accompanying text/audio/video entries do not count as separate elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Range of Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should showcase distinguished work by a single journalist (not a team) across the broad spectrum of content platforms and categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cover letter of up to 400 words may be submitted. Entrants must submit exceptional content from at least three different story topics or story types; you may submit up to five elements. Entries may include some content in which the nominee was not the sole contributor, but judges will give greater weight to entries and content by a single journalist. This category names winners in small, medium and large divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Type — general entry rules
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit on the number of entries per news outlet; however, any individual story may only be entered into one story type (which is separate from story topics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations compete against similarly sized organizations. Freelancers will be grouped based on the size of the outlet that published their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements per entry and element definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An entry shall consist of no more than three elements. An element can be a text, audio or video story, or an interactive. Accompanying photos and static graphics will not be counted as elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some categories (e.g., Breaking News outside general story-type rules) allow submitting multiple items as part of the entry; check specific category guidance. Elements are the primary units judges will evaluate; do not submit separate photos/graphics as elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter guidance (story type and topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover letter of up to 250 words is not required but may be submitted with your entry (story type/topic). For General Excellence and Best Range of Work, cover letters may be up to 400 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cover letters to give context — e.g., full day’s coverage plan for breaking news, description of an investigative package, or other explanatory details judges should consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commentary/Opinion (story type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported coverage that reflects the point of view of the journalist or news organization. Category includes unsigned editorials, individual columns and blogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should demonstrate clear, reported opinion or analysis; may include unsigned editorial pages or individual opinion columns/blogs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data (story type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners in this category will be recognized for exceptional content that is both premised on data and clearly and compellingly displays it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data-driven journalism should both rely on data analysis and present it in a compelling, understandable visual or narrative form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsletter (story type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that goes beyond a mere collection of links and informs and engages with the audience in a way that’s clearly meaningful and impactful to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsletters should show original reporting/analysis or curated context, not just aggregated links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast/Audio (story type) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that demonstrates excellence in audio storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Podcasts that show video of those speaking on camera may be entered in the Video category instead; content that relies on interviews or video not largely/entirely created in a studio should be entered in the Video category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video (story type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Online or television coverage that is visually compelling and deeply engaging, demonstrating excellence in visual storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes video-first storytelling; if a podcast includes significant video components, consider entering Video instead of Podcast/Audio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Topic — general entry rules
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit on the number of entries per news outlet; however, any individual story may only be entered into one story topic (which is separate from story types). An entry shall consist of no more than three elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories submitted to topic categories may also be submitted in other topic or type categories (subject to the single-entry-per-story-per-topic/type rule). Cover letter of up to 250 words is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Topic categories (list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined topic categories into which stories may be entered, including: Banking/Finance; Business of Sports; Economics; Energy/Sustainability/Climate; Government; Health/Science; International Reporting; Investing/Markets; Media/Entertainment; Personal Finance; Real Estate; Retail; Small Business; Technology; Travel/Transportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the topic category that best matches the subject matter; an individual story may be entered in only one story topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Journalism — eligibility and general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to undergraduate and graduate students. An entry shall consist of no more than three elements. Elements should represent the best work of the contributor(s) over the contest year. An element can be a text, audio or video story, or an interactive. Accompanying photos and static graphics will not be counted as elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cover letter of up to 250 words must be included that states whether each contributor is an undergraduate or graduate student, and the year of graduation (or expected graduation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Journalism — stories for professional news organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should focus on one student. The elements submitted can include other contributors, but all should primarily be the work of the entered student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover letter should address the contributions made to the entries by others; judges will evaluate primary authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Journalism — stories for student news organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should focus on one student. The elements submitted can include other contributors, but all should primarily be the work of the entered student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same guidance as for professional news organizations: cover letter should explain contributions by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Projects and Collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries can showcase work by more than one student, with minimal contributions from non-students. Entries should focus on one theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this category for collaborative student projects rather than single-student submissions; ensure non-student involvement is minimal and clearly explained in the cover letter.
